mainTopic: When an עולה becomes פסול: does the hide (עור) still go to the כהנים? The מחלוקת between רבי and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, and whether it matches the מחלוקת of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.
overview: The גמרא first explains that 'after הפשט' means after the animal became fit to be flayed, which is after זריקת הדם. It then quotes a ברייתא. רבי says the blood makes the hide acceptable on its own. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says the hide depends on the meat, but a פסול after זריקה still leaves the hide for the כהנים. The גמרא suggests that this matches the מחלוקת of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע about whether blood and meat depend on each other, but rejects the match. Both views can fit רבי יהושע, since he might agree the blood works when the כהנים would lose the hide, just as he agrees the blood works דיעבד. Next the גמרא defends רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים, who said he never saw a hide go out to be burned. It narrows his claim step by step to a stripped hide of a disqualified קרבן, and it shows that he holds the blood still works for a טריפה found in the inner organs, as רבי עקיבא learned from him. רבי יוחנן rules like רבי עקיבא, but only when an expert permitted the בכור. The final הלכה, however, follows the חכמים: the meat is buried and the hide is burned. The amud ends with a new משנה about where the burned bulls and goats are burned, and when they make clothing טמא.

steps.title: What does 'after flaying' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the phrase 'after הפשט' means in the statement it is discussing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what does 'after flaying' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what a phrase means. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read literally, 'after הפשט' would mean after the skin was actually removed. The גמרא is checking whether that is really the meaning, or whether it refers to some other moment.

keyTerms.meaning: Flaying: removing the hide from the animal
And what (does it mean)?

phrases.english: And what is 'after flaying'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this section by clarifying a term from the earlier discussion.

steps.title: It means before or after the animal became fit to be flayed
steps.stepSummary: 'Before/after הפשט' means before or after the animal became fit for flaying, which is the time of זריקת הדם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Before they became fit for flaying, and after they became fit for flaying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the dividing moment is when the animal became fit to be flayed, not when it was actually flayed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה may only be flayed after its blood has been put on the מזבח. So 'fit for הפשט' really means after זריקה. That turns the question into: did the פסול come before זריקה or after it?

keyTerms.meaning: That they became fit / were ready
Before

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'after הפשט' as 'after the skin was actually taken off.' It means after the moment the skin was allowed to be taken off, which is after זריקה.

phrases.english: before they became fit for flaying,
after they became fit for flaying.
phrases.notes: The animal becomes fit to be flayed once its blood has been put on the מזבח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The time marker is when the animal became fit for flaying, that is, the זריקה.

steps.title: What exactly are the two opinions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the details of the opinions of רבי and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the opinion of רבי, and what is the opinion of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks to hear the two opinions it has been referring to. This sets up a ברייתא that spells them out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their names came up earlier, but their positions were not yet explained. The גמרא now wants the source that lays them out.

phrases.english: What is the opinion of Rabbi
and what is the opinion of Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי רַבִּי וּמַאי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defining the time marker, the גמרא asks for the full opinions that use it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The content of each תנא's position.

steps.title: רבי: blood makes the hide acceptable on its own
steps.stepSummary: רבי holds that the blood makes the hide acceptable by itself. But if the hide is still on the meat when a פסול happens, the hide follows the meat, whether the פסול came before or after זריקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As taught in a ברייתא: רבי says the blood makes the hide acceptable by itself. When the hide is still with the meat and a פסול happens, whether before or after זריקה, the hide is treated like the meat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא giving רבי's opinion. If the hide was already removed, the blood alone lets it go to the כהנים. If the hide was still attached when the meat became פסול, the hide is burned along with the meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי, the hide counts as its own item that the blood can make acceptable. Once it is attached to meat that became פסול, though, it shares the meat's fate. The timing of זריקה makes no difference for him.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes acceptable (brings ריצוי)
By itself, on its own
Putting the blood on the מזבח
Like it: the hide follows the meat

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi says:

phrases.aramaic: הַדָּם מְרַצֶּה עַל הָעוֹר בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ.
phrases.english: The blood makes the hide acceptable by itself.

phrases.aramaic: וּכְשֶׁהוּא עִם הַבָּשָׂר, נוֹלַד בּוֹ פְּסוּל
phrases.english: And when it is with the flesh, and a disqualification arose in it

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין קוֹדֶם זְרִיקָה בֵּין לְאַחַר זְרִיקָה –
phrases.english: whether before sprinkling or after sprinkling –
it is like it.
phrases.notes: The hide gets the same treatment as the meat, so both are burned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 3 by quoting רבי's opinion.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The blood makes the hide acceptable alone. An attached hide follows the meat's פסול regardless of when the פסול came.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An attached hide is burned with the meat whether the פסול came before or after זריקה.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון: after זריקה the meat was accepted for a moment
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds that the blood cannot make the hide acceptable by itself. A פסול before זריקה makes the hide follow the meat. A פסול after זריקה still leaves the hide for the כהנים, because the meat was already accepted for a moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says: the blood does not make the hide acceptable by itself. If the hide is still with the meat and a פסול happens before זריקה, the hide is like the meat. After זריקה, the meat was already accepted for one moment, so he flays it and the hide goes to the כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the second opinion. For him, the hide only becomes acceptable through the meat. The timing of the פסול therefore matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the hide depends on the meat, what matters is whether the meat was ever accepted. If the פסול came after זריקה, the meat was acceptable for at least a moment, and that is enough to give the hide to the כהנים. If it came before זריקה, the meat was never accepted, so the hide is burned with it.

keyTerms.meaning: Was made acceptable
For one moment
He should flay it
To the כהנים

steps.whatToRemember: רבי: the blood makes the hide acceptable on its own, and an attached hide follows the meat no matter when the פסול came. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון: the hide depends on the meat, so a פסול after זריקה still leaves the hide for the כהנים.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין הַדָּם מְרַצֶּה עַל הָעוֹר בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ.
phrases.english: The blood does not make the hide acceptable by itself.
And when it is with the flesh –
if a disqualification arose in it before sprinkling,
it is like it.

phrases.aramaic: אַחַר זְרִיקָה, הוּרְצָה בָּשָׂר שָׁעָה אַחַת;
phrases.english: After sprinkling, the flesh was accepted for one moment;
he flays it, and its hide goes to the priests.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the same ברייתא, giving the opposing view.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The hide is acceptable only through the meat. A פסול after זריקה still gives the hide to the כהנים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פסול before זריקה means the hide is burned. A פסול after זריקה means the hide goes to the כהנים.

steps.title: Suggestion: is this the same as the מחלוקת of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון may be arguing over the same idea as רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say they disagree about the same thing as רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes linking this מחלוקת to an older, well-known one. This sets up the quote of that older מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לימא' signals a suggestion that the גמרא will test, and often turn down. The idea is that both מחלוקות may come down to whether the blood works on its own, without the meat.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (introduces a suggestion to be tested)
They disagree

phrases.english: Shall we say that in the dispute of Rabbi Eliezer
and Rabbi Yehoshua they disagree?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא בִּדְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to place the ברייתא's מחלוקת within a broader, earlier one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the hide מחלוקת is really the same as the מחלוקת about blood and meat depending on each other.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: no blood without meat, no meat without blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק and רבי יהושע's reading: blood and meat depend on each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And you shall offer your burnt offerings, the flesh and the blood.' רבי יהושע says: if there is no blood, there is no meat; if there is no meat, there is no blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins quoting the older מחלוקת, starting with רבי יהושע. He says the blood and the meat of an עולה cannot be offered without each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע reads 'the meat and the blood' as tying the two together. If one is missing or lost, the other cannot be offered either. This sounds like the view that blood alone cannot make something acceptable, which is close to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: Your עולות (burnt offerings)
If there is no…

phrases.english: 'And you shall offer your burnt offerings, the flesh and the blood' –
Rabbi Yehoshua says:
if there is no blood, there is no flesh,
phrases.notes: He means: if the blood can't be put on the מזבח, the meat can't be burned there either.

phrases.english: if there is no flesh, there is no blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins quoting the source of the parallel suggested in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהושע, blood and meat depend on each other: neither may be offered without the other.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: Blood is thrown even without meat
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר holds that the blood stands on its own and is thrown even when there is no meat. He reads the 'meat and blood' פסוק as teaching that the meat is tossed onto the מזבח, just like the blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: the blood is thrown even if there is no meat, because the פסוק says 'the blood of your sacrifices shall be poured.' Then why does the פסוק say 'you shall offer your burnt offerings, the meat and the blood'? To teach that just as blood is put on by throwing, the meat is also put on by tossing. So we learn that there is a gap between the ramp and the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא. Now we hear רבי אליעזר's side, which disagrees with רבי יהושע from the step before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע said blood and meat depend on each other. רבי אליעזר says the blood works alone, based on a different part of the פסוק. He then gives the 'meat and blood' phrase a new job: it teaches how the meat gets onto the מזבח (by tossing), not that the two depend on each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Throwing or tossing, the way the blood is put on the מזבח
What does the פסוק come to teach?
A gap or open space
The ramp leading up to the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר does not ignore the words 'the meat and the blood.' He uses them for something else: the way the meat is placed on the מזבח.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: דָּם – אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בָּשָׂר,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: the blood is thrown even though there is no meat,
as it says: 'And the blood of your sacrifices shall be poured out.'
If so, what does the verse come to teach when it says:
'And you shall offer your burnt offerings, the meat and the blood'?
phrases.notes: Same פסוק, earlier words. This is the phrase רבי יהושע used in step 7.

phrases.english: To tell you: just as the blood is put on by throwing,
so too the meat is put on by tossing.
So you have learned that a gap
exists between the ramp and the altar.
phrases.notes: The meat has to be tossed across that small gap, so it is 'thrown' just like the blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: דָּם – אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בָּשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in step 7 by giving רבי אליעזר's opposing reading of the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, the blood is thrown even when there is no meat. The phrase 'the meat and the blood' teaches that the meat is tossed, which shows there is a gap between the ramp and the מזבח.

steps.title: Proposed match: who follows whom
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the view that the hide is accepted follows רבי אליעזר, and the view that it is not accepted follows רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that the one who says the hide is accepted holds like רבי אליעזר, and the one who says it is not accepted holds like רבי יהושע?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now lines the two arguments up side by side. It is setting up a match that it will test in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the blood works without the meat (רבי אליעזר), it seems it should make the hide acceptable on its own. That is רבי's view. If blood and meat depend on each other (רבי יהושע), the blood cannot work alone, which sounds like רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (a suggestion that is often rejected)
It was accepted. Here it means the blood made the hide acceptable for the כהנים.
The one who says

phrases.aramaic: לֵימָא מַאן דְּאָמַר הוּרְצָה – כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר,
phrases.english: Shall we say that the one who says it was accepted holds like Rabbi Eliezer,
phrases.notes: The one who says 'accepted' is רבי, from step 4.

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאן דְּאָמַר לֹא הוּרְצָה – כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ?
phrases.english: and the one who says it was not accepted holds like Rabbi Yehoshua?
phrases.notes: The one who says 'not accepted' is רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, from step 5.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא מַאן דְּאָמַר הוּרְצָה – כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out exactly how the suggestion from step 6 would work, now that both views have been quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the argument between רבי and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון match the argument between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע?

steps.title: Rejected: the argument fits only רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the match. If we follow רבי אליעזר, both would agree the hide is accepted. Their argument is only about what רבי יהושע would say.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי אליעזר, everyone agrees. Where they argue is according to רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proposed match. It says the two sides are not split between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי אליעזר lets the blood work without meat, even רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון would agree that the hide is accepted under his view. So the real argument must be about how to understand רבי יהושע.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the view of
Everyone agrees
Where they do argue

phrases.aramaic: אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר – כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי;
phrases.english: According to Rabbi Eliezer, everyone agrees;
phrases.notes: Agrees that the hide is accepted, since for him the blood works even without the meat.

phrases.english: where they argue is according to Rabbi Yehoshua.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר – כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the match proposed in step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that רבי sides with רבי אליעזר and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון sides with רבי יהושע.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Under רבי אליעזר there is no argument at all. Both views can be explained within רבי יהושע's opinion.

steps.title: How both views fit רבי יהושע: the כהנים' loss
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון follows רבי יהושע in the simple way. רבי says that רבי יהושע only spoke about meat, where the כהנים lose nothing. With the hide, they would lose, so רבי יהושע would agree the blood works.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says it is not accepted follows רבי יהושע simply. The one who says it is accepted will tell you: רבי יהושע only said his rule there about meat, where the כהנים lose nothing. But with the hide, where the כהנים do lose something, even רבי יהושע agrees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how each side can hold like רבי יהושע. This finishes the rejection from step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע's rule that blood needs meat was said in a case where only meat was involved. Losing that does not hurt the כהנים. The hide is a gift to the כהנים, so רבי argues that רבי יהושע would let the blood work in order to save it for them.

keyTerms.meaning: He only said his rule this far, meaning his statement is limited to that case
A loss
Agrees

steps.whatToRemember: The argument between רבי and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון is not רבי אליעזר against רבי יהושע. Both fit רבי יהושע. They only argue about whether his rule changes when the כהנים would lose the hide.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common move in the גמרא: a rule may be limited to the case where it was said. Here, a possible loss to the כהנים could change the result.

phrases.aramaic: מַאן דְּאָמַר לֹא הוּרְצָה – כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ.
phrases.english: The one who says it was not accepted holds like Rabbi Yehoshua.
The one who says it was accepted will tell you:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הָתָם –
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua only said his rule there
about meat, where there is no loss to the priests;
but with the hide, where there is a loss to the priests,
even Rabbi Yehoshua agrees.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר הוּרְצָה אָמַר לָךְ: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills out the claim from step 10 by showing how each view fits רבי יהושע.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: רבי יהושע's rule applies only where the כהנים would lose nothing.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהושע's rule that blood depends on meat seemed to rule out רבי's view that the hide is accepted.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהושע spoke only about meat, where the כהנים lose nothing. When the hide is at stake, he may agree that the blood works, so רבי can hold like him too.

steps.title: Support from the case where the blood was already thrown
steps.stepSummary: רבי's reading of רבי יהושע is just like the known case of דיעבד. There, רבי יהושע agrees that if the blood was thrown after the meat became impure or disqualified, the קרבן is accepted.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is just like the case of 'after the fact.' As we learned: if the meat became impure or disqualified, or went out beyond the curtains, רבי אליעזר says the כהן should throw the blood, and רבי יהושע says he should not. But רבי יהושע agrees that if he already threw it, the קרבן is accepted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to support רבי's view from step 11: even רבי יהושע admits the blood works once it has already been thrown.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even when the meat is ruined, רבי יהושע only says not to throw the blood from the start (לכתחילה). If it was thrown anyway, he agrees it counts (הורצה). So the blood still has real power without the meat, and that power can be enough to give the כהנים the hide.

keyTerms.meaning: After the fact; once it has already been done
The curtains that marked off the courtyard of the משכן
He should throw (the blood on the מזבח)
It is accepted; the קרבן did its job

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how רבי can say that רבי יהושע would accept the blood for the hide: רבי יהושע already admits the blood counts when it has been thrown.

phrases.english: It is just like the case of 'after the fact';
as we learned:
If the meat became impure or was disqualified,
or if it went out beyond the curtains,
רבי אליעזר says: he should throw the blood;
רבי יהושע says: he should not throw it.

phrases.aramaic: וּמוֹדֶה רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ שֶׁאִם זָרַק – הוּרְצָה.
phrases.english: And רבי יהושע agrees that if he did throw it, the offering is accepted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי's explanation in step 11 by pointing to an accepted teaching.
steps.raayaObject: רבי's claim that, according to רבי יהושע, the blood works to give the כהנים the hide.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching that רבי יהושע agrees הורצה if the blood was thrown after the meat was ruined.

steps.title: Challenge to רבי חנינא: some hides are always burned
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים, who said he never saw a hide go out to be burned. It asks: what about the bulls and goats that are burned whole, together with their hides?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים said, and so on. Did he really never see it? What about the bulls that are burned and the goats that are burned?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and quotes רבי חנינא. Then it challenges his claim right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some קרבנות, the פרים הנשרפים and שעירים הנשרפים, are burned outside together with their hides as part of how they are normally done. A כהן in the בית המקדש would surely have seen that. So how could רבי חנינא say he never saw a hide go out to be burned?

keyTerms.meaning: The deputy כהן גדול
Bulls whose bodies are burned outside the camp
Goats whose bodies are burned outside the camp
And did he not?! (a challenging question)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא סְגַן הַכֹּהֲנִים כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: רבי חנינא, the deputy כהן גדול, said, and so on.
phrases.notes: The 'and so on' points back to the משנה: 'In all my days I never saw a hide go out to the place of burning.'

phrases.english: And did he not see it?!
But there are the bulls that are burned
and the goats that are burned!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא?! הֲרֵי פָּרִים הַנִּשְׂרָפִים וּשְׂעִירִים הַנִּשְׂרָפִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line in the משנה, the statement of רבי חנינא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא's claim that he never saw a hide go out to be burned.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: פרים הנשרפים and שעירים הנשרפים are always burned with their hides, so he must have seen hides being burned.

steps.title: He did not mean hides burned as part of the מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא was not talking about hides that are burned as part of the normal מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are not talking about burning that is part of their מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing what רבי חנינא meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burning the hide of the פרים הנשרפים is simply the way that קרבן is done. רבי חנינא meant he never saw a hide burned because the קרבן was disqualified.

keyTerms.meaning: As part of their מצוה; the normal way they are done
We are saying; we are talking about

phrases.english: We are not talking about burning that is part of their מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי חנינא meant he never saw any hide burned at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: He meant he never saw a hide burned because the קרבן was disqualified.

steps.title: Challenge: an offering disqualified before skinning
steps.stepSummary: Sometimes a קרבן is disqualified before it was skinned and before the blood was thrown, and then it is burned with its hide. Surely רבי חנינא saw that.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about a קרבן disqualified before skinning and before the blood was thrown?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges again, even after the narrower reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the קרבן became disqualified before the הפשט and before the זריקה, everyone agrees the whole animal is burned with its hide. That is burning because of disqualification, not as a מצוה. So the narrower reading still does not fully explain רבי חנינא's claim.

phrases.english: But there is a case of before skinning and before the blood was thrown!
phrases.notes: If the קרבן is disqualified at that point, the animal is burned together with its hide.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The narrowed reading: he never saw a hide burned because of disqualification.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קרבן disqualified before skinning and before the blood was thrown is burned with its hide, so he would have seen that.

steps.title: He meant a hide that was already stripped off
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא meant he never saw a stripped hide go out to be burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are talking about a stripped hide.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final answer and narrows רבי חנינא's statement even more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal burned whole, with its hide still on, does not count. רבי חנינא only meant that he never saw a hide that had already been skinned off sent out to be burned.

keyTerms.meaning: Stripped; a hide already removed from the meat

steps.whatToRemember: רבי חנינא's statement is about a hide already stripped off a disqualified קרבן. It is not about hides burned as a מצוה, and not about hides burned while still on the animal.

phrases.english: We are talking about a stripped hide.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Further narrowing the scope of the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He meant any hide burned because of disqualification, even one still on the animal.
steps.terutzMaskana: He meant only a hide already stripped off the meat.

steps.title: A case where a stripped hide should be burned
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, an animal disqualified after flaying but before the blood was thrown would have its stripped hide burned. So רבי חנינא should have seen this.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is the case of an animal disqualified after flaying and before the blood was thrown! According to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who says the blood does not bring acceptance for the hide by itself, that stripped hide is burned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 16 with a case where a hide that was already stripped would go out to be burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds that throwing the blood cannot make the hide permitted if the meat is already disqualified. So if the animal became disqualified after the skin came off but before the blood was thrown, the stripped hide must be burned. That is exactly what רבי חנינא said he never saw.

phrases.english: But there is the case after flaying
and before the throwing of the blood
phrases.notes: He means the animal became disqualified during that window: the skin was already off, but the blood was not yet thrown.

phrases.english: according to Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon
who says: the blood does not bring acceptance
for the hide by itself!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer from step 16, that רבי חנינא meant a stripped hide
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא's claim that he never saw a stripped hide burned
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's view, a stripped hide is burned when the animal is disqualified after flaying but before the blood is thrown.

steps.title: רבי חנינא follows רבי
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא holds like רבי, who says the blood does bring acceptance for the hide by itself, so that hide is not burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא holds like רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי חנינא simply does not hold like רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. He holds like רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי, throwing the blood makes the hide permitted even when the meat is already disqualified. So in that case the hide goes to the כהנים and is not burned, and the challenge falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds (this opinion)

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina
holds like Rabbi.
phrases.notes: This is רבי's view from step 4: the blood works for the hide by itself, even if the meat became disqualified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17 by assigning רבי חנינא to the opposing opinion
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the speaker to a different תנא's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי חנינא might hold like רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון
steps.terutzMaskana: He holds like רבי, so that hide is never burned

steps.title: In practice, flaying never comes before the blood
steps.stepSummary: Even under רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון the case never happens, since everyone agrees the animal is not flayed before the blood is thrown.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say this: even if you explain him like רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, רבי agrees that flaying does not come before the throwing of the blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer, so that רבי חנינא can fit even רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order of the עבודה is to throw the blood first and only then remove the skin. So a hide is never already stripped while the blood is still waiting to be thrown. That means רבי חנינא never had a chance to see such a case.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (a second answer)
You explain it (as following this opinion)
Agrees

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
even if you explain it
like Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon –
Rabbi agrees
that flaying does not come before the throwing of the blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא אֲפִילּוּ תּוֹקְמַהּ כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: The case does not happen in practice
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An animal could be flayed before its blood is thrown
steps.terutzMaskana: Flaying is always done after the blood is thrown, so the case never comes up

steps.title: A טריפה discovered in the inner organs
steps.stepSummary: What about an animal found to be a טריפה in its inner organs after it was flayed? That animal was already unfit when the blood was thrown, so its stripped hide should be burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is the case where the animal was found to be a טריפה in its inner organs!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises another case where a stripped hide should seemingly go out to be burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the blood was thrown and the skin removed in the right order. But afterward the animal was found to have a fatal wound inside. That means it was unfit all along, so the blood seemingly never worked, and the stripped hide would need to be burned.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a fatal injury or defect, which makes it unfit
The inner organs, intestines

phrases.english: But there is the case where it was found to be a טריפה
in the inner organs!
phrases.notes: This is found only after flaying, when the animal is opened up, so the skin is already off.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to רבי חנינא's claim
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא's claim that he never saw a stripped hide burned
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A טריפה found after flaying was unfit when the blood was thrown, so its stripped hide should be burned.

steps.title: The blood still works for a hidden טריפה
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא holds that when an animal is found to be a טריפה in its inner organs, the blood still brings acceptance, so the hide is not burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that if it was found to be a טריפה in the inner organs, the blood brings acceptance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that in רבי חנינא's view, this case does not cause the hide to be burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the animal was really a טריפה, the throwing of the blood still counts and makes the hide permitted. So the hide goes to the כהנים, and רבי חנינא's claim still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds

phrases.english: He holds: if it was found to be a טריפה in the inner organs –
the blood brings acceptance.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר נִמְצֵאת טְרֵיפָה בִּבְנֵי מֵעַיִים מְרַצֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the speaker's position on the הלכה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A hidden טריפה makes the blood useless, so the hide is burned
steps.terutzMaskana: The blood still brings acceptance, so the hide goes to the כהנים

steps.title: Proof from רבי עקיבא's words in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה supports this. רבי עקיבא learned from רבי חנינא that if a בכור was flayed and then found to be a טריפה, the כהנים may still use its hide.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is exact too, since it teaches: רבי עקיבא said, from his words we learned that if someone flays a בכור and it is found to be a טריפה, the כהנים may benefit from its hide. Learn from this that it is so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for its answer from the משנה itself and accepts the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא drew a lesson from רבי חנינא's statement: a flayed animal later found to be a טריפה still gives its hide to the כהנים. That only makes sense if the blood brings acceptance in such a case. So this fits exactly with what step 21 said רבי חנינא holds.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is exact too (it supports this)
A firstborn animal, brought as a קרבן
That they may benefit
Learn from it (the proof is accepted)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי חנינא never saw a stripped hide burned. Either he holds like רבי, or flaying never comes before the blood. And a טריפה found in the inner organs still lets the blood work, as רבי עקיבא learned from him.

phrases.english: The wording is exact too –
since it teaches: Rabbi Akiva said:
from his words we learned,
phrases.notes: "His words" means רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים's statement in the משנה.

phrases.english: that one who flays the firstborn
and it is found to be a טריפה –
the priests may benefit from its hide!
Learn from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דַּיְקָא נָמֵי דְּקָתָנֵי אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 21
steps.raayaObject: That in רבי חנינא's view, the blood brings acceptance for a טריפה found in the inner organs
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי עקיבא's statement in the משנה about a flayed בכור found to be a טריפה
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The proof is accepted: the hide of a hidden טריפה goes to the כהנים

steps.title: What does רבי עקיבא add?
steps.stepSummary: If רבי חנינא already taught the rule, רבי עקיבא's statement seems to add nothing new.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, what is רבי עקיבא teaching us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reading from the last step. If this is what רבי חנינא meant, why does רבי עקיבא need to say anything?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 explained that for רבי חנינא, the blood still brings acceptance for an animal that is a טריפה inside, so the hide is not burned. If so, רבי עקיבא's report of the same idea seems to be extra. The גמרא wants to know what new point he is making.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? What is new here?
But then (if so)

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶלָּא מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא?
phrases.english: But then, what is Rabbi Akiva teaching us?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof from the משנה in step 22, saying רבי עקיבא's statement seems unnecessary.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for רבי עקיבא's statement in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי חנינא's rule already covers this case, then רבי עקיבא repeating it adds nothing.

steps.title: The rule applies even outside the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא teaches that the rule applies even in גבולין, outside the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he teaches us: the rule applies even outside the מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי עקיבא adds something new. The rule works even for a בכור slaughtered outside the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inside the מקדש, throwing the blood is what lets the כהנים keep the hide. A בכור with a מום is slaughtered outside, where no blood is thrown. רבי עקיבא teaches that there, the slaughter does the same job: if the animal is found to be a טריפה only after slaughter, the hide still goes to the כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: Places outside the מקדש (and outside ירושלים)
This is the new point he teaches us

phrases.english: This is what he teaches us:
even in the outlying areas.
phrases.notes: He means a בכור with a מום, which is slaughtered outside the מקדש and not offered as a קרבן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the statement a wider reach: it covers a new setting.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא's statement only repeats רבי חנינא's rule about the מקדש.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי עקיבא extends the rule to גבולין, where the slaughter takes the place of the blood.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן rules like רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that the הלכה follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the הלכה follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא gives a practical ruling. The הלכה follows רבי עקיבא, so the hide of such a בכור goes to the כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the גמרא was explaining what רבי עקיבא's view means. Now רבי יוחנן decides that, in practice, we follow it.

keyTerms.meaning: The final ruling follows...

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
The halakha follows Rabbi Akiva.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that רבי עקיבא's view is clear, this step gives a ruling on it.

steps.title: Only when an expert permitted the בכור
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא's rule applies only if an expert approved the מום before slaughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even רבי עקיבא only said this when an expert permitted the animal. If no expert permitted it, the hide is not allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits רבי עקיבא's rule. The slaughter only permits the hide if an expert first checked the מום and allowed the בכור to be slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור may only be slaughtered outside the מקדש after an expert confirms it has a real מום. Without that approval, the slaughter was not a proper slaughter. So it cannot do the job of permitting the hide.

keyTerms.meaning: An expert who checks whether a בכור's מום is real
Permitted it (to be slaughtered)

phrases.english: And even Rabbi Akiva said this only
when an expert permitted it,
but if an expert did not permit it, then no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לֹא אָמַר אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the ruling of step 25 to the case where an expert approved the בכור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaughter permits the hide only when an expert permitted the בכור first.

steps.title: Final ruling: the meat is buried and the hide is burned
steps.stepSummary: The final הלכה follows the חכמים: the meat is buried and the hide is burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה follows the חכמים: the meat is buried, and the hide is burned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final ruling, and it goes against רבי עקיבא. The hide does not go to the כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים in the משנה said that רבי חנינא's 'I never saw it' is not a proof. For them, a בכור found to be a טריפה does not give its hide to the כהנים, even if it was already skinned. So the meat must be buried and the hide must be burned.

keyTerms.meaning: And the final הלכה is
Burial
Burning

steps.whatToRemember: In the end, the הלכה follows the חכמים. A בכור found to be a טריפה after skinning does not give its hide to the כהנים: the meat is buried and the hide is burned.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two rulings. Step 25 quoted רבי יוחנן ruling like רבי עקיבא, but the גמרא's final word here follows the חכמים.

phrases.english: And the halakha follows the words of the Rabbis;
the flesh is buried, and the hide is burned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Overrides רבי יוחנן's ruling and decides like the חכמים.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The hide of a בכור found to be a טריפה is burned, and its meat is buried.

steps.title: New משנה: where the burned bulls and goats are burned
steps.stepSummary: Burned bulls and goats burned the proper way go to בית הדשן and make clothing טמא; if burned because they became unfit, they are burned in the בירה and do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The bulls and goats that are burned: when they are burned the proper way, they are burned in בית הדשן and make clothing טמא. If they are not burned the proper way, they are burned in the בירה and do not make clothing טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts a new topic. It compares bulls and goats burned the proper way with ones burned because they became unfit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some bulls and goats, like those of יום כיפור, are meant to be burned after their blood is thrown. When burned properly, this is done outside ירושלים in בית הדשן, and the clothing of the people who burn them becomes טמא. If they became unfit and are burned for that reason, they are burned in the בירה, and the clothing stays טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: Bulls whose bodies are burned instead of eaten
Goats whose bodies are burned instead of eaten
The proper way, as commanded
The ash place outside ירושלים
The burning place in the בירה (the area of the מקדש)
Make the clothing (of those who burn them) טמא

steps.whyThisMatters: The same animal can have different laws depending on whether its burning is the proper מצוה or just disposal of something unfit.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Bulls that are burned
and goats that are burned,
when they are burned the proper way,
are burned in the place of the ashes
and make clothing impure,
and if they are not burned the proper way,
they are burned in the burning place of the bira
and they do not make clothing impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Burned properly: burned in בית הדשן and makes clothing טמא. Burned because unfit: burned in the בירה and does not make clothing טמא.
